plain: Following one after another in order, with no break between

webster.text: Following in order or uninterrupted course, as a series of persons or things, and either in time or place; as the successive revolutions of years or ages; the successive kings of Egypt.

example.quote: The more powerful members, instead of being kept in awe and subordination, tyrannized successively over all the rest.
example.cite: The Federalist No. 18 (Madison, with Hamilton), Dec. 7, 1787
